entities.summary:
Lodovico Piavi, OFM was a Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem. Born in unknown year and died on January 24, 1905. He served as the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem from 1892 until his death in 1905. During this time, he worked to promote unity among Christians in Jerusalem and played a significant role in the city's religious and cultural landscape.

Piavi was a prominent figure in the Catholic Church and was recognized for his efforts to rebuild and restore the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem after years of destruction during the Ottoman period. He also oversaw the construction of several important buildings, including the Basilica of St. John the Baptist and the Convent of the Franciscans.

Despite facing challenges from other Christian denominations in the city, Piavi remained committed to his faith and continued to work towards reconciliation among Christians.

Piavi's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a key role in shaping the modern Catholic Church's presence in Jerusalem. His efforts helped to establish the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem as a major center for Christian worship and learning, and paved the way for future generations of clergy and laity to serve in the city.

Today, Piavi is remembered as a pioneering figure in the history of the Catholic Church in Jerusalem, whose dedication and perseverance helped to bring stability and unity to the city's religious community.
